point: Stored the normal 16-bit way, the 2.8-trillion-setting model is 5.6 TB — it would take 70 top-end 80GB accelerators just to hold it. Squeezing each setting to ~4 bits cuts the model to 1.5 TB (19 accelerators), a ~4× drop, while the numbers stay 99.2% faithful to the originals. Honest surprise from our run: MXFP4 is NOT more accurate than plain 4-bit integers here (12.396% error vs 10.774%) — its power-of-two shared scale wastes a little range. MXFP4 wins for a different reason: that power-of-two scale is almost free to apply in hardware and 4-bit floats run natively on the tensor cores, so it's faster and cheaper to serve at the same size. (Per-weight error isn't end-task accuracy: real serving also keeps the few most sensitive parts at higher precision.)
